workflow_runs.display_title: fix(33): the ELF architecture check ran before the archives were copied

head_commit.message:
fix(33): the ELF architecture check ran before the archives were copied

Run 36555370299, both llama.cpp jobs, step "Build":

    [198/198] Linking CXX static library src/libllama.a
    FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'dist/lib/libllama.a'
    ##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.

The BUILD SUCCEEDED. llama.cpp compiled and linked all 198 targets, and then the
check I added to verify the result tried to read a file that did not exist yet.

dist/lib is populated by the NEXT step -- "Package with headers" runs
`cp "$S" "dist/lib/$(basename "$S")"` for every archive it finds under build/.
The Build step only ever produces build/src/libllama.a. So a check for the
architecture of the packaged archives was placed one step before they are
packaged.

This is the same shape of mistake as the circular CMake check: the assertion was
written where it was convenient to write it rather than where the thing it
inspects comes into existence. Moved into "Package with headers", immediately
after the cp loop, and verified that in the parsed YAML the copy precedes the
check:

    check now in step: Package with headers | cp to dist/lib precedes it: True

workflow_runs.name: android-deps
workflow_runs.display_title: fix(32): gs_llama_chat called llama.h symbols outside the feature guard

head_commit.message:
fix(32): gs_llama_chat called llama.h symbols outside the feature guard

Run 36553404233 failed every ABI at step 3, the host type-check, before any
Android work:

    llama_wrapper.cpp:449:20: error: 'llama_chat_apply_template' was not
      declared in this scope
    llama_wrapper.cpp:449:70: error: request for member 'size' in 'msgs',
      which is of non-class type 'int'
    error occurred in cc-rs: command did not execute successfully (status 1):
      LC_ALL="C" "c++" "-O0" ...        <- the HOST compiler

THE WRAPPER IS COMPILED ON HOSTS WITH NO LLAMA.CPP AT ALL

llama_wrapper.cpp is added to the cc::Build unconditionally and compiled whether
or not a llama.cpp tree is present. Only the llama.h USES sit behind
`#if defined(GS_LLAMA_HAVE_LLAMA)`, which build.rs defines when a tree exists. My
gs_llama_chat was the one function outside that guard, so on a host with no
llama.h it referenced four undeclared symbols.

The second error is the first one seen twice: with `llama_chat_message` unresolved,
`std::vector<llama_chat_message> msgs;` stops parsing as a declaration and `msgs`
becomes an int. Chasing the `msgs` error would have wasted the run.

The body is now inside `#if defined(GS_LLAMA_HAVE_LLAMA)` with the same named
"libllama not linked" failure the rest of the file uses in the #else branch, so
the no-llama host build and the no-llama runtime path now report the same thing.

VERIFIED HERE, NOT ONLY IN CI: the host build really does compile the wrapper
(the log above shows c++ being invoked), so `cargo check -p gs-ffi
--features jni-typecheck` exercises the #else branch directly. 163 tests still
pass.
